parsed.summary: The Lean file states that Mathlib's riemannZeta is nonzero for every complex s with Re s > 7/8. This is the ζ-only case (character modulo 1) of the paper's main theorem. The statement includes s = 1, where riemannZeta takes a junk convention value, but that value is nonzero, so the claim is true there as well.

glossary.plain: Mathlib's Riemann zeta function, the meromorphic continuation of ζ(s) to ℂ, totalized at s = 1
glossary.note: At s = 1, Mathlib uses the convention value (γ - log 4π)/2. This is nonzero, so the nonvanishing claim there is harmless.

glossary.plain: Re s > 7/8, a strict inequality, with 7/8 computed as a real number
glossary.note: The cast is explicit `(7/8 : ℝ)`, so there is no truncating division.

lean_claims.plain: For every complex s with Re s > 7/8, riemannZeta s ≠ 0.

paper_claims.plain: Every finite-order Hecke L-function over Q(√-3) and every Dirichlet L-function, including ζ, has no zero in Re s > 7/8. A pole at s = 1 for a principal character is allowed.
The quasi-Riemann hypothesis holds with σ₀ = 7/8: nontrivial zeros of ζ have real part at most 7/8.

coverage.why: This is exactly ζ ≠ 0 on Re s > 7/8. The pole at s = 1 is not a zero, and Mathlib's value there is nonzero.

coverage.paper_ref: Theorem 1.1, Dirichlet L-functions and Hecke L-functions over Q(√-3)
coverage.why: The formal target covers only ζ, not the general Dirichlet or Hecke cases.

flags.explanation: Only the ζ special case of the main theorem is formalized. The Dirichlet L-function and Hecke L-function parts are absent. This is a scope limit, not a mismatch.

The region Re s > 7/8 contains the pole s = 1, where riemannZeta equals the convention value (γ - log 4π)/2. The Lean statement also asserts this value is nonzero, which the paper does not say. The value is nonzero, so the extra claim is true and harmless.

lint_verdicts.why: 7/8 is typed as a real number, so it is the true 0.875 and not truncated.
The pole at s = 1 is covered, but Mathlib's convention value there is nonzero, so the statement is still true and faithful.
Same as above: riemannZeta 1 ≠ 0, so the extra claim at the pole is true.
